title: RegTrack: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Multi-Class Legal Change Detection
key_contributions: First published benchmark for fine-grained legal change detection
4,772 manually annotated EU regulation provision pairs
Atomic Legal Units (ALUs) as the unit of comparison
6-class taxonomy: no_change, syntactic_change, reference_update, semantic_change, addition, deletion
Demonstrates LLM classification dominates (91.6% F1) but alignment is the bottleneck (combined 56.8%)

key_result.insight: LLMs excel at isolated change classification (91.6% Macro-F1) but fail at end-to-end alignment+classification (56.8% combined). Domain-specific dense encoders offer more robust pipeline performance.

direct_implication_for_skill: Validates the 3-pass alignment strategy: (1) mechanical title-similarity pairing, (2) LLM verification of pairs, (3) meaning-based resolution of unmatched items. Shows item numbers are unreliable anchors; wrong pairings produce plausible but false semantic shifts.
resolution_requirement_for_downstream: When aligning provisions between versions, always validate pairing before classification. A high-confidence but false alignment can contaminate the entire analysis.
reading_notes: Critical validation of the skill's design. Shows the 54.5% → ~7% error reduction in PRISMA case is not just incremental improvement but fundamental architectural necessity. Recommend reading Table 2 (results) and Section 6 (discussion of alignment vs classification tradeoff).
